findings.finding: Classic accumulating/replacing eligibility traces retain per-state/action temporal credit across steps and are a foundational delayed-reward baseline rather than a novel mechanism.
sources: Singh & Sutton, Reinforcement Learning with Replacing Eligibility Traces, Machine Learning 22 (1996), DOI 10.1007/BF00114726

findings.finding: Three-factor synaptic learning and e-prop combine local eligibility traces with delayed modulatory/learning signals; biological reviews through 2025 report experimental support for seconds-scale eligibility traces.
sources: Izhikevich, Solving the distal reward problem through linkage of STDP and dopamine signaling, BMC Neuroscience 2007
Gerstner et al., Frontiers in Neural Circuits 2018, DOI 10.3389/fncir.2018.00053

findings.finding: ICLR 2026 Cascading Eligibility Traces explicitly address event-mixing in standard exponentially decaying traces and provide temporally precise delayed-credit memory over seconds to minutes.
sources: Ralambomihanta et al., Learning From the Past with Cascading Eligibility Traces, ICLR 2026

findings.finding: Temporal eligibility and selective causal responsibility should be separated prospectively: future tests should put recency/eligibility in conflict with actual responsibility and require ordinary trace baselines before counterfactual-responsibility interpretation.
